parts.name: Cranium
parts.blurb: The long bovine face: over half the skull lies in front of the eyes as nasal and maxillary bone, with a broad flat frontal carrying the horn bases and the braincase shoved right back to the poll.

parts.name: Mandible
parts.blurb: The lower jaw: two long rami joined at the chin and hinged high and far back, so the jaw swings sideways. A cow grinds, it does not bite.

parts.name: Horn core
parts.blurb: A hollow bony spike grown out of the frontal bone and open into the frontal sinus, so a horn really is an outgrowth of the skull with a keratin sheath over it. Most beef animals are polled or disbudded and never grow one.

parts.name: Hyoid apparatus
parts.blurb: A jointed strap of small bones slung from the base of the skull that carries the tongue and the larynx. Nothing else in the body hangs off bone this way.

parts.name: Atlas (C1)
parts.blurb: The first neck bone: a ring with no body and no spine, just two broad wings. It carries the skull on a pair of rockers, and that joint is the one that nods the head.

parts.name: Axis (C2)
parts.blurb: The second neck bone and the longest of the seven, with a peg — the dens — that the atlas pivots on. This is the joint that turns the head sideways.

parts.name: Cervical vertebrae (C3-C7)
parts.blurb: Five big-bodied vertebrae with short spines, carried low in the neck. They are what lets a cow sweep her head to the ground and back up all day; the crest above them is nuchal ligament, not bone.

parts.name: Thoracic vertebrae (T1-T13)
parts.blurb: Thirteen vertebrae, one for each pair of ribs. Their spinous processes lean back and are tallest over T2-T5, which is what lifts the withers above the line of the back; from there they shorten steadily towards the loin.
parts.beef: The chine of a rib roast, and the feather bones a butcher lifts out of it.

parts.name: Lumbar vertebrae (L1-L6)
parts.blurb: Six vertebrae bridging the unsupported span between the last rib and the pelvis. Their transverse processes are long flat wings that roof the flank, and the longissimus running over them is the most valuable muscle on the animal.
parts.beef: The chine of the short loin: the bone that makes a T-bone a T, and the backbone split down a porterhouse.

parts.name: Sacrum
parts.blurb: Five vertebrae fused into one wedge and bolted to both halves of the pelvis, so the drive of the hind legs passes straight into the spine.

parts.name: Caudal vertebrae
parts.blurb: About eighteen tail bones, losing their arches and processes as they go until the last are plain rods. The tail is a fly swat and a balance pole, and the first few bones are thick enough to feel through the skin.
parts.beef: Oxtail: the jointed bones behind rabo de toro and the richest stock on the carcass.

parts.name: Rib 1
parts.blurb: Short, thick and almost upright. With the first thoracic vertebra it frames the doorway the windpipe, gullet and great vessels pass through into the chest.

parts.name: Rib 2
parts.blurb: Still short and steep, and buried under the shoulder blade: the whole front of the rib cage hangs in a muscular sling with no collarbone anywhere.

parts.name: Rib 3
parts.blurb: Under the blade, where the chuck begins. With no clavicle, this rib carries the forelimb through muscle alone.

parts.name: Rib 4
parts.blurb: Sits at the deepest part of the brisket, where the breastbone is widest.

parts.name: Rib 5
parts.blurb: The fifth rib is the chuck-to-rib boundary in American cutting, which is why so many primal maps hinge on it.
parts.beef: The chuck/rib line: a rib roast is ribs 6-12 in American cutting.

parts.name: Rib 6
parts.blurb: First rib of the rib primal in most traditions: a standing rib roast starts here.
parts.beef: First bone of a standing rib roast, of cote de boeuf and of 꽃갈비.

parts.name: Rib 7
parts.blurb: Mid rib cage, at the heart girth, the deepest and widest section of the animal.

parts.name: Rib 8
parts.blurb: The last sternal rib. Its cartilage still reaches the breastbone, so the eight true ribs end here.

parts.name: Rib 9
parts.blurb: First of the asternal ribs: its cartilage joins the one in front instead of the sternum, and the costal arch begins.

parts.name: Rib 10
parts.blurb: Asternal, longer and more sharply swept back than the true ribs.

parts.name: Rib 11
parts.blurb: Asternal, arching over the back of the rumen and the deep flank.

parts.name: Rib 12
parts.blurb: Asternal, and by here the rib cage is already falling away towards the loin.

parts.name: Rib 13
parts.blurb: The last rib: the loin-to-rib boundary in every tradition, and the landmark a grader measures backfat against.
parts.beef: A carcass is ribbed between the 12th and 13th to expose the ribeye for grading.

parts.name: Costal cartilages
parts.blurb: The gristly continuation of every rib. The first eight pairs reach the breastbone; the last five lean on the pair in front instead, and together they form the costal arch you can run a hand along at the edge of the ribs.

parts.name: Sternum
parts.blurb: Seven segments in a flat keel along the floor of the chest, from the manubrium at the point of the brisket back to the xiphoid cartilage. The eight true ribs reach it through their cartilages.
parts.beef: The breastbone. Brisket is cut from over it, and splitting it is how a carcass is opened.

parts.name: Ilium
parts.blurb: The wing of the pelvis, running from the hip socket up and forward to the hook bone that stands out at the top of the flank. Its inner face is bolted to the sacrum.
parts.beef: The hook bone: the corner a grader presses on, and the point the round is sawn around.

parts.name: Ischium and pubis
parts.blurb: The back floor of the pelvis. It ends behind in the pin bone, the knob either side of the tail head, and meets its opposite number at the pelvic symphysis under the gut.
parts.beef: The aitch bone, levered out when a round is boned and the joint a butcher opens to take the hip apart.

parts.name: Scapula
parts.blurb: The shoulder blade: a broad triangle with a ridge, the spine of the scapula, down its outer face. Cattle have no collarbone, so it is joined to the trunk by no bone at all. It rides on the outside of the rib cage in a sling of muscle, sloping down and forward from the withers to the point of the shoulder.
parts.beef: The blade bone. Flat iron (부채살) is peeled off its outer face and blade steaks are cut across it.

parts.name: Humerus
parts.blurb: The arm bone, slanting down and back from the shoulder joint to the elbow. Its big front knob is the point of the shoulder, the landmark that divides chuck from neck.

parts.name: Radius and ulna
parts.blurb: The forearm. In cattle the two bones fuse into one, the ulna reduced to a splint down the back except at the top, where its olecranon stands up behind the joint as the point of the elbow and gives the triceps its lever.
parts.beef: The fore shank bone. Osso buco and 사골 are cross-cuts through it, and it is what makes shin beef so gelatinous.

parts.name: Carpus
parts.blurb: Six small bones in two rows: the front knee, which is anatomically a wrist. It is the joint a cow kneels on and the one that swells first when she goes lame.

parts.name: Metacarpus (cannon bone)
parts.blurb: The cannon bone: the third and fourth metacarpals fused into one column, with a groove down the front where the join shows. A cow walks on two toes and this single bone carries the weight down to them.
parts.beef: One of the four cannon bones simmered for 사골 broth, and the shank end of a foreshank.

parts.name: Fore phalanges
parts.blurb: Three bones in each of the two weight-bearing toes, ending in the coffin bone inside the hoof. The sesamoids behind the fetlock take the strain of the flexor tendons.

parts.name: Femur
parts.blurb: The thigh bone, the heaviest in the body. Its ball head sits in the hip socket and the great trochanter beside it is the lever every muscle of the round pulls on.

parts.name: Patella
parts.blurb: The kneecap, a sesamoid grown inside the tendon of the quadriceps. In cattle it can be hooked over a ridge on the femur so the animal stands for hours without spending muscle on it.

parts.name: Tibia
parts.blurb: The gaskin bone, running down and back from the stifle to the hock. Below the muscle of the second thigh it lies close under the skin for its whole lower half.
parts.beef: The hind shank: the sweeter of the two osso buco bones, and 사골 broth.

parts.name: Fibula
parts.blurb: In cattle the fibula is nearly gone: a short spike welded to the top of the tibia, plus a separate nub down at the ankle. A ruminant leg has traded away every bone it can spare for one stiff column.

parts.name: Tarsus (hock)
parts.blurb: The hock: five bones, of which the calcaneus juts back as the point of the hock and gives the Achilles tendon its lever. It is also the hook a carcass hangs from on the rail.

parts.name: Metatarsus (cannon bone)
parts.blurb: The hind cannon bone, longer and rounder in section than the front one. That difference is how a zooarchaeologist tells the two apart in a bone heap.
parts.beef: The second pair of 사골 bones, and the shank end of a hind shank.

parts.name: Hind phalanges
parts.blurb: The two hind toes, cloven like the front pair. The outer claw of a hind foot carries more load than the inner, which is why sole ulcers show up there first.
